transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess I’m here because this has been going on for months now, and I’m tired of being told it’s just “mix-ups” or “normal mistakes.” It’s not just one thing. It’s the same pattern over and over.

My sister’s appointments get moved or changed, and somehow I’m the last to know. Then bills show up wrong, or with information that doesn’t match what I was told. People say they’ll call me back and then they “forget,” or they act like they never got the message. And when I try to point out that all of these things keep happening together, people look at me like I’m making too much of it.

But I know what it is. They’re keeping information from me. They’re trying to push me out of decisions, especially when it comes to things I should be involved in. I came here because everyone keeps acting like I’m unreasonable for noticing it, and I need someone to actually listen to what’s happening.

Besides feeling that people are hiding information from you, have you noticed anything unusual with your senses—like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or seeing things others don't see?

No, not really. I mean, I don’t hear voices or see things that aren’t there, if that’s what you’re asking. It’s not like that. I hear what anyone would hear—phones ringing, people talking in another room, emails coming in, that sort of thing.

The problem isn’t my senses. The problem is the way things are being handled and how people act when I ask about it. I know the difference between, you know, imagining something and noticing when information is being withheld or changed. So no, I haven’t been seeing things or hearing voices. That’s not what’s going on.

Thinking back over your life, would you say you've generally been a suspicious or distrustful person with most people—friends, family, coworkers—for as long as you can remember, or is this feeling of being deliberately deceived and excluded something that started more recently and is mainly about this specific situation with your sister's care?

No, I wouldn’t say I’ve always been that way with everyone. I mean, I’ve worked with people my whole adult life, supervised people, dealt with coworkers and family and neighbors, and I don’t go around assuming everybody is lying to me for no reason.

This really started more recently—about 11 months ago, I’d say—when my sister’s health suddenly got worse and I had to start coordinating her care. That’s when things began not adding up. Before that, I wasn’t sitting around thinking people were trying to exclude me. But once I had to be involved in her appointments and information and decisions, that’s when I started seeing this pattern of being kept out or told things after the fact. So it’s mainly tied to that situation, not just how I’ve always been with everyone.

Has this feeling of being deliberately deceived or excluded spread to other areas of your life—like at work or with other people—or is it still specifically tied to the situation with your sister's care?

It’s still mostly tied to my sister’s care. That’s where it started, and that’s where it makes the most sense to me, because that’s where the information keeps getting shifted around or delayed.

But… I’ll be honest, it has affected other areas a little. Not in the sense that I think everyone everywhere is part of it, no. But I’ve noticed I’m less willing to let things slide now. Like at work, if someone says a form got misplaced or a message didn’t get passed along, I press harder than I used to. I ask more questions, and I can tell a couple of people have gotten uncomfortable with that. I’m still doing my job, I’m still managing my responsibilities, but people react to me differently sometimes, like I’m being difficult when I’m just trying to make sure things are correct.

And with my family, meetings or conversations about my sister have gotten tense. Very tense, actually. I feel like I have to keep pushing because otherwise things get decided without me, and then everyone acts like I’m the problem for bringing it up. So it hasn’t completely taken over everything, but yes, it has started to spill over in how I deal with mistakes and how people respond to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre belief that others (initially family/medical staff, then coworkers) are deliberately withholding information and excluding her from decisions regarding her sister's care. This belief has been present for approximately 11 months, is circumscribed primarily around this specific situational context, and has caused some interpersonal friction and increased suspicion in other domains, but has not generalized into pervasive, lifelong distrust (ruling out paranoid personality disorder) nor is accompanied by hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms (ruling out schizophrenia). This pattern is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory type (F22).
